outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to LLMs in Tabular Learning
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by defining the domain of tabular learning, introducing the concept of few-shot learning, and discussing the rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) as potential tools for this task. It contrasts current limitations with the proposed solution.
subtopics: The Challenge of Few-Shot Learning in Tabular Data: Why traditional methods struggle with limited labeled data.
The Promise of LLMs: Leveraging world knowledge and reasoning capabilities for data analysis.
Limitations of Current LLM-based Tabular Approaches: High inference costs per sample, API-only access constraints (no fine-tuning), and prompt size bottlenecks.
Introducing FeatLLM: A paradigm shift from end-to-end prediction to 'Feature Engineering via Reasoning'.
High-Level Roadmap of the FeatLLM Framework.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Theoretical Foundations and Problem Formulation
outline.description: Before diving into the mechanics, this chapter establishes the mathematical and conceptual framework required to understand how rules are translated into machine-readable features for probabilistic inference.
subtopics: Problem Definition: Formalizing the classification task with labeled samples, features, and class descriptions.
From Natural Language to Boolean Logic: The concept of translating human-readable 'rules' into binary feature indicators.
Probabilistic Inference via Linear Models: How simple models (e.g., Logistic Regression) can be trained on synthetic binary features to estimate class likelihoods.
The Role of Weights: Understanding how trainable weights represent the importance of generated features versus hardcoded logic.
Why Ensemble Methods? The theoretical basis for combining multiple imperfect models to achieve robustness (Bagging principles applied to LLM output).

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Architecture of FeatLLM – Rule Extraction via Prompt Engineering
outline.description: This is the core methodological chapter detailing how FeatLLM instructs an LLM to act as an expert feature engineer. It breaks down the specific prompt components designed to elicit high-quality causal rules from noisy text data.
subtopics: Prompt Design Philosophy: Guiding Chain-of-Thought reasoning step-by-step.
Sub-task 1: Basic Information Description – Structuring feature definitions, types, and few-shot examples effectively.
// Sub-task 2 // Prior Knowledge Activation – Separating general reasoning from data-specific patterns to avoid spurious correlations.
// Sub-task 3 // Deductive Rule Derivation – Explicit guidance on generating logical conditions (If/Then) that distinguish classes.
// Output Formatting // Ensuring parseable structure for automated rule extraction despite LLM noise.
// Design Choices Explained // Why we fix a specific number of rules per class and how feature types constrain generation.
